title: Apportion token billing for streamed multi-tenant requests with intermittent KV hits
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Background: Streaming request flows sometimes interleave model token generation with KV/prefix cache hits. In multi-tenant batches we observe cases where some stream frames are satisfied entirely from cache (zero model tokens) and others require model execution, and the current accounting attributes cost to the whole batch or to the first requester, causing unfair quota burns and surprising billing reports.

Problem: Two main incorrect behaviors have been reported: (1) quota/rate-limit windows charging based on aggregated batch size rather than per-tenant chargeable tokens, leading to early throttles for tenants who mostly hit cache; (2) billing that charges token units for frames satisfied by prefix/KV cache in some batch fusion paths. Both cause customer confusion and incorrect quota enforcement.

Goal: Implement an attribution algorithm that: (A) charges only the model-executed token units to tenants; (B) apportion batch-level GPU cost (when we bill per-batch or per-slot) across tenants by a defensible heuristic when requests are fused; (C) ensures rate limits and quota counters reflect chargeable tokens (not attempted tokens that were short-circuited by cache). This should preserve latency SLOs and be implementable without blocking streaming optimization paths.

Proposed approach:
1) Instrument per-request token accounting at the runtime boundary that distinguishes: attempted_tokens, cache_served_tokens, model_generated_tokens.
2) Charge tokens toward customer quota and rate-limit counters using model_generated_tokens only.
3) For GPU/billing attribution when batch fusion happens across tenants, compute a proportional apportionment: allocate the batch GPU time and per-batch overhead cost in proportion to model_generated_tokens per tenant in that fused batch. If model_generated_tokens == 0 for all tenants (unlikely but possible for cache-only batch), fall back to equal-split or attribute to tenant that initiated the RPC (configurable).
4) Handle streaming frames: maintain a lightweight per-stream accumulator that updates as cache hits or model gen occur; billing and quota updates are committed periodically (end-of-stream or on configured checkpoint), with ability to push interim deltas to reduce tail risk.
5) Backfill and reconciliation: for historical batches where we overcharged, provide a reconciliation pipeline that replays runtime accounting logs and emits adjustments to billing/quotas.

Engineering notes:
- This requires runtime hooks in the batching layer to tag per-subrequest token counts prior to coalescing into physical batches and to propagate attribution metadata to the metering pipeline.
- The metering pipeline must accept per-request delta updates (incremental counters) rather than only batch-level totals.
- To avoid perf regressions, tag propagation should be compact (8-16 bytes per subrequest) and optional behind an opt-in config for early rollout.

Trade-offs and alternatives:
- Simpler option: treat any fused batch as charged to the initiator (fast to implement, but unfair). Rejected.
- Conservative option: continue charging on attempted_tokens for quota enforcement and issue credits later. This avoids under-enforcing quotas in real time but perpetuates early throttles.
- Chosen approach favors correctness for customers while keeping an emergency fallback to conservative enforcement if telemetries show evasion or abuse.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes per-subrequest counters: attempted_tokens, cache_served_tokens, model_generated_tokens
Quota and rate-limit counters increment only by model_generated_tokens in both single-tenant and fused-batch paths
Billing records (per-invoice line) reflect model_generated_tokens and proportional batch-cost apportionment for fused batches
Integration tests simulating mixed cache-hit ratios validate that tenant A with 90% cache hits is not throttled earlier than tenant B with 10% cache hits under same request rate
Reconciliation job can locate and emit adjustments for misattributed charges for a given two-week window
Rollout gated by telemetry thresholds: no >1% request latency regression and <0.1% increase in metering pipeline CPU/memory cost in first 48h
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): enable tag propagation and per-request delta reporting for 5% of hosted accounts in us-west1 for 72h. Verify telemetry thresholds. Phase 2 (expand): 25% rollout and enable proportional apportionment for fused batches with reconciliation dry-run enabled (no live refunds). Phase 3 (full): 100% rollout, enable reconciliation actions and billing adjustments, and update SDK/Docs. Each phase has rollback toggles and a kill-switch to revert to attempted_tokens enforcement.
sdk_and_docs_impact: Update SDK docs to explain that quotas are charged on model-generated tokens and add guidance on expected behavior for streaming + caching. Add server-side feature flagging API. Update billing FAQ with example scenarios and reconciliation procedure.
migration_plan: 1) Short-term: opt-in config for early adopters. 2) Mid-term: default-on for hosted customers; notify Dedicated customers 4 weeks in advance with migration notes for on-prem runtime patches. 3) Long-term: include attribution metadata in exportable billing CSVs and update customer billing UI to show cache-saved tokens per invoice.
